run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T02:47:21Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is explained at the frontend-proxy layer: the proxy intermittently returns 503 on its own ingress requests because its upstream cluster `frontend` terminates the HTTP connection before a response starts (Envoy response flag UC, `upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}`). frontend-proxy `ingress` STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were present from the earliest available sample (minute ending 02:18:48) through 02:56, at 2-6 spans per minute with one 14-span burst in the minute ending 02:41:48, i.e. the alert fires on low-volume intermittent error spans rather than a sustained outage. All 21 pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts and all 21 deployments are 1/1 available, so a crash/OOM/eviction cause is not supported. The frontend-side reason the connections are closed could not be observed (frontend container logs empty, no frontend error traces retrievable), the proxy's Envoy configuration is not exposed, and the RequestErrorRate rule definition is not loaded in this Prometheus, so the exact expression behind the reported value 0.0111111 remains unknown. No pre-incident baseline exists because every pod in the stack started at 02:06:54Z.

claims.text: At 02:47:21Z frontend-proxy's own spans carried a nonzero error rate: `ingress` with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.0037 spans/s and `router frontend egress` STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0, with `ingress` STATUS_CODE_UNSET at 10.07 spans/s and `router frontend egress` UNSET at 10.08 spans/s over the 5m lookback 02:42:21-02:47:21Z.

Sampled frontend-proxy error traces (data range 02:21:06-02:34:59Z) share one shape: an `ingress` span with tags error=True, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR whose child `router frontend egress` span carries error="true" and http.status_code="0"; the affected trace roots are load-generator operations user_browse_product, user_view_cart, user_get_recommendations, user_get_ads and user_add_to_cart.

Whole trace b303e7616d6cc9296844951cbe4749d5 contains only 4 spans (load-generator user_browse_product, load-generator GET 503, frontend-proxy `ingress` 503, frontend-proxy `router frontend egress` error/http.status_code 0); no span from the `frontend` service appears in that trace.

frontend-proxy access logs record the failures as `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` against upstream cluster `frontend`: 02:21:06.645Z and 02:21:06.746Z for `GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N` and `GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO`, 02:24:08.297Z for `GET /api/products/LS4PSXUNUM`, and 02:34:59.946Z for `GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO`.

The failure is per-connection and transient: in the window 02:24:05-02:24:10Z `GET /api/products/LS4PSXUNUM` returns 503 UC at 02:24:08.297Z and the same URL returns `200 - via_upstream` (535 response bytes, 533 ms) at 02:24:09.285Z.

Per-minute increase of frontend-proxy `ingress` STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans is intermittent: 4 in the minute ending 02:18:48, 2-6 in scattered minutes (02:25:48, 02:28:48-02:29:48, 02:33:48-02:38:48, 02:48:48-02:49:48, 02:55:48-02:56:48), 0 in many minutes, and a single burst of 14 in the minute ending 02:41:48, which also shows 12 `router frontend egress` error spans and 10 `frontend` `GET` error spans.

The `frontend` service has its own error-status spans but no nonzero gRPC client error rates at the alert time: over the 10m ending 02:47:21Z, `frontend` span_name `GET` had STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 0.00877 spans/s, while grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem, AdService/GetAds and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder all had error rate 0.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with restart count 0, including frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw (startTime 02:06:54Z) and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56 (startTime 02:06:55Z); no container shows a lastState terminated reason or exit code.

All 21 deployments in otel-demo report DESIRED 1, AVAILABLE 1, READY 1 and UPDATED 1; frontend runs ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend, frontend-proxy :2.1.3-frontend-proxy and product-catalog :2.1.3-product-catalog.

Kubernetes events in otel-demo contain only a controller-driven product-catalog rolling update: Deployment product-catalog scaled replica set product-catalog-55f64b54c9 from 0 to 1 and product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0 at 02:39:56-02:40:00Z, with ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate of pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 and SuccessfulDelete of pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp; no FailedScheduling, Unhealthy, BackOff or Evicted events were returned.

Pod IPs are frontend-proxy 100.96.3.19, frontend 100.96.3.42 and load-generator 100.96.3.52, so in the access-log lines the trailing 100.96.3.52:port field is the load-generator client and the upstream is identified by the literal cluster field `frontend`.

No comparable pre-incident baseline is available: the 1h-increase query for frontend/frontend-proxy error and UNSET spans across the authorized day returned a single point for the final hour (frontend-proxy `ingress` error 28.36 vs UNSET 28300.23; frontend `GET` error 5.06 vs UNSET 22113.92), consistent with all pods having started at 02:06:54Z.

Sampled traces of the `frontend` service near 02:35:51Z are healthy - every frontend `GET` span carries http.status_code 200 or 308 and every gRPC client span on those traces has rpc.grpc.status_code 0 - and frontend-proxy `ingress`/`router frontend egress` spans on the same traces carry http.status_code 200 or 308.

The `flagd-config` ConfigMap in otel-demo currently sets `productCatalogFailure` to defaultVariant "on" (description "Fail product catalog service on a specific product") while other chaos flags such as adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are "off".

product-catalog's own spans in the hour ending 02:57:21Z carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 26429 spans, oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts 2294 spans); no product-catalog span with STATUS_CODE_ERROR appears in that series.

Only two metric series names exist for the frontend-proxy service in this Prometheus: traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, i.e. the service exposes only trace-derived metrics.

Primary cause: frontend-proxy's 503s are generated by its upstream `frontend` terminating HTTP connections before a response starts (Envoy UC `upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}`). Because the failures are per-connection and sporadic (2-14 per minute against about 10 ingress spans/s), the same URL succeeds one second later, the frontend pod shows 0 restarts and no terminated container state, and sampled frontend traffic is all 200/308, the most plausible mechanism is connection-level churn (for example an upstream HTTP keep-alive/idle-timeout race) rather than an application outage; the precise frontend-side trigger is not observable in this Run.

Secondary, correlation-only: the single error burst (14 frontend-proxy `ingress` error spans plus 12 egress and 10 frontend `GET` error spans in the minute ending 02:41:48Z) falls 48-108 s after the product-catalog single-replica rolling update at 02:39:56-02:40:00Z, so that rollout is a candidate contributor to that burst; it cannot account for the errors recorded from the minute ending 02:18:48Z onward, and no trace or log evidence from the burst minute is available to confirm it.

Alternative candidate not supported by the observed failure mode: the `productCatalogFailure` flag set to "on" is designed to fail product-catalog for a specific product, and the sampled failing requests are product routes (`GET /api/products/{id}`). However the proxy recorded a connection reset before any upstream response rather than an error response, product-catalog emitted no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, and product-page requests were succeeding during the window, so the evidence does not tie this flag to the 503s; which product the flag targets could not be verified.

Pod crash, OOMKill, eviction or capacity shortage in otel-demo is rejected as the cause: all 21 pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts and no lastState terminated reason or exit code, all 21 deployments have AVAILABLE/READY/UPDATED = 1, and the only events returned are the product-catalog rollout's Scheduled/SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete/ScalingReplicaSet/Killing entries.

The product-catalog rollout at 02:39:56-02:40:00Z is rejected as the explanation of the alert: frontend-proxy `ingress` error spans were already counted in the minute ending 02:18:48Z, roughly 21 minutes earlier, errors continue afterwards, and the rollout is a controller-driven ReplicaSet scale-up/scale-down (SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete), not damage.

Against a sustained frontend failure: sampled `frontend` traces near 02:35:51Z contain only 200/308 HTTP statuses and rpc.grpc.status_code 0 client calls, the URL that failed with 503 UC at 02:24:08.297Z returned `200 - via_upstream` at 02:24:09.285Z, and frontend-proxy access logs for 02:42:58-02:42:59Z show a stream of `200 - via_upstream` responses for /api/cart, /api/data, /api/products/*, /api/recommendations and /api/checkout.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule definition is unavailable: list_prometheus_rules returned status no_data with 0 rules for both rule_name=RequestErrorRate and the unfiltered listing, so the expression, window and denominator behind the reported value 0.01111111111111111 are unknown.
No pre-incident baseline exists (all pods created 02:06:54-02:08:43Z), so whether this error rate is new or chronic cannot be determined; the 1h-increase query returned only the final-hour point.

The frontend-side cause is unknown: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw read 0 bytes for 02:20-03:07Z and for 02:34:55-02:35:10Z (status no_data), traces_search for service `frontend` in 02:40-02:52Z returned no traces (status no_data), and traces_search_by_tags for `frontend` with error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and http.status_code=503 each returned no matching traces (status no_data), so the frontend's own STATUS_CODE_ERROR `GET` spans could not be inspected.
A frontend `GET` http.status_code=500 search returned no matching traces (status no_data), so the status classes behind the frontend error spans are not established.

The frontend-proxy Envoy configuration is not exposed: the namespace ConfigMaps are only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products, so upstream idle timeout / connection-pool settings that would confirm a keep-alive race could not be checked.

No HTTP-level metric series exist for frontend-proxy: get_metric_names for {__name__=~"http_.*"} and an http_server_request_duration_seconds_count query on frontend-proxy both returned status no_data, and only traces_span_metrics_* series exist, so no request/status-code counters (including any ERROR counter) are available - absence here is unknown, not zero.
An rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count query for service_name=frontend returned status no_data, so the frontend's gRPC client status distribution is not available from that metric.

Traces for the 02:40:48-02:41:48 burst are not retrievable (traces_search_by_tags for frontend-proxy error=true in 02:41:40-02:43:00Z returned no matching traces), so the burst is evidenced only by span metrics.

A broad traces_search for service frontend in 02:00-03:07:48Z returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE (476 rows, 90681 tokens) and was not paged through, so the full frontend span set for the window was not reviewed.
A filtered read of the product-catalog container log for 02:30-02:45Z returned no matching err|error|fail|exception|panic|warn lines (status no_data), which is not proof that no such line existed.
The flagd `productCatalogFailure` target product and toggle time cannot be read beyond the ConfigMap value, and no change history integration is available.
Downstream/customer impact beyond the sampled load-generator GET 503 spans was not quantified.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the alerting/recording-rule source, since it is not loaded in this Prometheus, to confirm the metric, window and denominator producing 0.0111111.
Review frontend-proxy's Envoy cluster and route configuration (upstream idle timeout, connection-pool reuse, per-route timeout) against the frontend HTTP server keep-alive timeout and align them.

Collect frontend application output from a log backend or file rotation (its container emitted no stdout in the window) and capture one failing request's frontend-side view to identify why the socket closes before a response.
Confirm with the team owning the demo chaos flags whether `productCatalogFailure` targets the product IDs on the failing routes (2ZYFJ3GM2N, 9SIQT8TOJO, LS4PSXUNUM).
